decision: DIFFERS -> W2 + W6. Two cited pages BOTH name Asian pear and BOTH state a MINIMUM, and they disagree: NCSU Table 15-5 has its own row 'Pears, Asian | 20' (a single minimum, 20 ft) and clemson_hgic asian-pear states "Plant trees at least 10 to 15 feet apart in fall or early spring." (a minimum stated as a RANGE). This is not a scope argument: NCSU's row is Asian-pear-specific too. It is W2 as refined: a stated minimum authors as the point UNLESS another cited page for the crop states a range, in which case the range wins and the minimum is noted. Clemson's sentence is the range -> in_row [120,180], 'minimum' recorded; NCSU's 20 ft minimum is noted and sits above the range (the two pages disagree, W6: one page's figure is authored, never a value joined from both). Secondary: Clemson's is a recommending sentence in a crop factsheet; NCSU's is a cross-fruit table cell. UC ANR's 12 ft / rows 17-18 ft is commercial (200 trees per acre), not authored (W4). No row figure (not_authored). Today's [144,300] matches no page. The crop keeps its open R4 blocking finding (PLA-579), unrelated to this field. The 16 scanner hits are fruit-thinning distances (6 in), fire-blight cut lengths and a pollinizer distance: none restates plant spacing.
